microtheory.name: business_management
microtheory.definition: Business management + organization. Strategy, operations, marketing, finance, accounting, HR, organizational behavior. Drucker, Porter, Mintzberg, Christensen, Senge. The discipline of running organizations effectively. Substrate analogue: how groups of agents coordinate to achieve coherent purpose under resource constraints.

concepts.name: firm_business
concepts.definition: Organization producing goods or services. Coase 1937: exists because internal coordination cheaper than market transactions when transaction costs high.

concepts.name: corporation
concepts.definition: Legal entity separate from owners. Limited liability. Publicly traded vs privately held. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-organizational pattern.

concepts.name: stakeholder
concepts.definition: Anyone affected by firm: shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers, community. Vs narrow shareholder-primacy view.

concepts.name: fiduciary_duty
concepts.definition: Duty to act in another's interest. Officers + directors to shareholders. Foundation of corporate governance.

concepts.name: strategy_business
concepts.definition: Long-term plan for achieving competitive advantage. Porter's 5 forces + generic strategies (cost leadership, differentiation, focus).

concepts.name: porter_five_forces
concepts.definition: Michael Porter 1979. Industry attractiveness determined by: rivalry, new entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power.

concepts.name: competitive_advantage
concepts.definition: Sustained above-normal returns. From cost leadership, differentiation, or focus. Source must be hard to imitate.

concepts.name: blue_ocean_strategy
concepts.definition: Kim + Mauborgne. Create uncontested market space rather than compete in existing markets. Cirque du Soleil.

concepts.name: disruptive_innovation
concepts.definition: Clayton Christensen. New entrants serve underserved segments with simpler/cheaper products, then move upmarket displacing incumbents.

concepts.name: resource_based_view
concepts.definition: Barney 1991. Sustainable competitive advantage from valuable, rare, inimitable, non-substitutable resources (VRIN).

concepts.name: marketing
concepts.definition: Identifying + satisfying customer needs profitably. 4Ps: product, price, place, promotion. Kotler.

concepts.name: market_segmentation
concepts.definition: Dividing market into distinct customer groups with different needs. STP: segmentation, targeting, positioning.

concepts.name: brand
concepts.definition: Identifier + associations + promises customers attach to product/firm. Source of premium pricing + loyalty.

concepts.name: customer_lifetime_value
concepts.definition: CLV. Net present value of customer over relationship. Foundation of customer-centric strategy.

concepts.name: operations_management
concepts.definition: Design + management of production systems. Inventory, quality, supply chain, capacity.

concepts.name: lean_manufacturing
concepts.definition: Toyota Production System. Eliminate waste (muda). Just-in-time. Continuous improvement (kaizen). Substrate analogue: substrate's parsimony drive.

concepts.name: six_sigma
concepts.definition: Quality methodology. <3.4 defects per million. DMAIC: define, measure, analyze, improve, control.

concepts.name: supply_chain
concepts.definition: Network from raw material to end consumer. Logistics, sourcing, distribution.

concepts.name: bullwhip_effect
concepts.definition: Demand variability amplifies upstream in supply chain. Information sharing reduces.

concepts.name: finance_corporate
concepts.definition: Capital structure, investment decisions, dividend policy. NPV, IRR, WACC.

concepts.name: net_present_value
concepts.definition: NPV. Sum of future cash flows discounted to present. Decision rule: accept if NPV > 0.

concepts.name: weighted_average_cost_capital
concepts.definition: WACC. Blended cost of equity + debt financing. Discount rate for unlevered free cash flows.

concepts.name: capital_structure
concepts.definition: Mix of debt + equity financing. Modigliani-Miller theorem + corrections (taxes, distress costs).

concepts.name: accounting
concepts.definition: Recording + reporting financial transactions. GAAP vs IFRS. Three statements: balance sheet, income, cash flow.

concepts.name: double_entry_bookkeeping
concepts.definition: Each transaction recorded in two accounts (debit + credit). Pacioli 1494. Self-checking.

concepts.name: balance_sheet
concepts.definition: Snapshot: assets = liabilities + equity at point in time.

concepts.name: income_statement
concepts.definition: Revenue + expenses + profit over period. P&L.

concepts.name: organizational_structure
concepts.definition: Functional, divisional, matrix, network. Trade-offs between specialization + integration.

concepts.name: bureaucracy_weber
concepts.definition: Weber: hierarchy + rules + impersonal + meritocratic + specialised. Ideal type. Strengths + dysfunctions.

concepts.name: organizational_culture
concepts.definition: Schein. Artifacts → values → underlying assumptions. Strong cultures align behavior; mismatches destroy mergers.

concepts.name: transformational_leadership
concepts.definition: Bass + Burns. Leaders raise followers' motivation + morality. Contrast with transactional.

concepts.name: human_resources
concepts.definition: Recruiting, training, evaluating, compensating workforce. Strategic vs administrative views.

concepts.name: agency_problem_corporate
concepts.definition: Jensen + Meckling 1976. Managers (agents) may pursue interests divergent from shareholders (principals). Governance + incentive design correct.

concepts.name: learning_organization
concepts.definition: Peter Senge. Fifth discipline. Systems thinking + mental models + shared vision + team learning + personal mastery.

rules.name: firms_exist_because_transaction_costs
rules.head: Jabberwock asks why organizations form rather than markets alone
rules.body: Coase 1937: when market transaction costs exceed internal coordination costs, firms emerge. Substrate's coordination-cost principle.

rules.name: five_forces_determine_industry_profitability
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates an industry's attractiveness
rules.body: rivalry + entrants + substitutes + buyer power + supplier power jointly determine sustained profitability. Porter 1979.

rules.name: disruptive_innovation_starts_low_end
rules.head: Jabberwock observes new market entrants
rules.body: disruptive innovations enter at underserved segments with simpler products, then move upmarket displacing incumbents. Christensen.

rules.name: agency_costs_require_incentive_alignment
rules.head: Jabberwock has principals + agents with divergent interests
rules.body: incentive design (equity, performance pay) + monitoring align interests. Jensen + Meckling 1976.

rules.name: culture_eats_strategy
rules.head: Jabberwock implements organisational change
rules.body: Drucker (attributed): culture eats strategy for breakfast. Underlying assumptions trump formal plans. Substrate's deep-pattern resistance.
